official.deadline_note: Two dates per cycle: early admission deadline 15 December 2026, by which CMU-Africa covers competency test fees and offers complimentary Duolingo (DET) coupons to eligible first-time applicants, and final application deadline 15 January 2027 after which applications close and cannot be edited. Applications received after the early deadline are only considered if submitted with valid DET/IELTS/TOEFL scores. There is no separate deadline for the scholarship itself - consideration follows admission plus the financial aid assessment form.
official.application_cycle: Fall 2027 entry cycle: applications opened 1 October 2026, applications are reviewed January-April 2027, decisions are shared April-May 2027, the Student Induction Program runs May-August, and the semester begins in September 2027.
official.status_note: CMU-Africa's homepage and how-to-apply page state 'Applications for CMU-Africa are open!' and 'Applications are open!', with all programme applications open since October 1 for the fall 2027 intake; the admissions FAQ is marked 'Updated for fall 2027 application'.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Program 'covers ... tuition and fees' and CMU-Africa states that 'in addition to full tuition coverage' it provides a range of tailored resources. CMU-Africa's published 2026-2027 tuition is USD 16,000 for African students and USD 61,510 for international students.

official.application_route: Apply through CMU's graduate admissions portal for MSIT, MS ECE or MS EAI, then complete CMU-Africa's separate financial aid assessment form; scholarship consideration follows admission.
official.study_mode: Full-time, in-person; no part-time tracks; fall semester entry only, with the semester beginning in September after the May-August Student Induction Program.
official.citizenship_residency: Only admitted applicants of African nationality are eligible for CMU-Africa financial aid, which includes the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
official.international_eligibility: International students may be admitted to CMU-Africa programmes, but only admitted applicants of African nationality are eligible for financial aid, so this Programme is effectively limited to African nationals.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Admission to one of CMU-Africa's Master of Science programmes - MSIT, MS ECE or MS EAI; programmes are tailored for candidates with a strong background in computer science or engineering, and GRE is not required for admission purposes.
official.duration: MSIT: 16-20 months (3-4 semesters); MS EAI: 16-20 months (3-4 semesters); MS ECE: 10-16 months; programme includes a mandatory three-month master's internship (MSIT).
official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at CMU-Africa, established in 2016 as part of a global network of 33 Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partners, supports highly talented, service-oriented young people who face the highest social and economic barriers to opportunity. Scholars complete a Master of Science in Information Technology, Electrical and Computer Engineering, or Engineering Artificial Intelligence at CMU-Africa in Kigali and receive comprehensive, wrap-around academic, personal and professional support from selection through to employment or further education.
official.program_type: Fully funded need-based graduate scholarship at Carnegie Mellon University Africa in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no standalone scholarship application to file: you must first win admission to CMU-Africa's MSIT, MS ECE or MS EAI in Kigali, then complete the separate financial aid assessment form that places you in contention for the Programme. The award covers full tuition and fees (2026-2027 African-student tuition USD 16,000), health insurance, travel and basic living expenses, and adds career preparation, leadership development and entrepreneurship support through graduation. Treat 15 December 2026, not 15 January 2027, as the operative deadline: only applicants who apply by the early deadline get their competency test and Duolingo English Test fees covered, and later applications are only reviewed with valid DET/IELTS/TOEFL scores already submitted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African nationals with a strong computer science or engineering background, demonstrable financial need and a track record of community contribution who can commit to a full-time, in-person master's in Kigali.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft essays early: MSIT/MS EAI require three 300-word essays (fourth optional) and MS ECE a statement of purpose, all plus a single unedited 3-minute video essay recorded in English on Chrome or Firefox.
Confirm three recommenders and their working email addresses before starting the portal form; MS ECE letters arrive through a portal link, MSIT/MS EAI references are contacted directly by admissions.
Prepare transcripts as one PDF with the grading scale/key attached and check that the name on your ID or passport matches your application and test-provider accounts.
If targeting the 15 December early deadline, book the Duolingo English Test early and have scores sent directly to CMU-Africa, since DET fee coverage is limited to eligible first-time applicants.
Complete the financial aid assessment form as soon as it appears on your application status page; only applicants who file it are considered for need-based aid and the Programme.
common_rejection_risks: Applying after 15 December without valid English scores attached, or self-reporting TOEFL/DET scores, which CMU-Africa does not accept.
Assuming the scholarship is a separate application - files that never submit the financial aid assessment form are not considered for need-based aid.
Thin technical preparation: CMU-Africa states its programmes are tailored for candidates with strong CS/engineering backgrounds and that others are unlikely to succeed.
Plagiarised statements of purpose (grounds for denial), plus avoidable document failures such as a CV over two pages, multi-file or uninterpretable transcripts, and inactive recommender emails.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Program covers tuition, fees, health insurance, travel and basic living expenses; CMU-Africa's published estimate for monthly living costs is USD 345-580 (housing, food, transport, connectivity, personal care), so anything above basic living expenses plus discretionary and family commitments must be funded by the scholar.
document_audit: Transcripts must be uploaded as a single PDF with the grading scale/key/back page attached - only unofficial transcripts are needed to apply, but an uninterpretable grade scale is the classic fixable failure.
Self-report IELTS in the portal with the TRF number; TOEFL (institution code 2074) and DET must be sent by the testing agency and can fail to link if names or emails differ from the application.
Keep the CV at two pages or fewer as a PDF and verify each recommender's current email - MS ECE letters are submitted by recommenders through a portal link.
Use one consistent legal name across the admission application, the financial aid assessment form, the ID/passport upload and all English test accounts.
alerts: December 15, 2026 is the effective deadline: later applications are only considered with valid DET/IELTS/TOEFL, and first-time applicants lose covered competency test and DET fees.

The Programme has no independent deadline or application form - consideration follows admission plus the financial aid assessment form, and only African nationals can receive CMU-Africa financial aid.
Only one programme application per cycle is allowed, entry is fall-only with no part-time option, so plan for a 10-20 month relocation to Kigali.
GRE is not required, and CMU-Africa admits holistically with no GPA cut-off, but a weak technical background is the quiet reason many otherwise complete applications stall.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account in CMU's graduate admissions portal, submit the application (essays, video essay, CV, references, transcripts) by the deadline, sit the one-hour technical test when invited, then complete the financial aid assessment form on the status page to enter aid and Scholars Program consideration.
